Carrick denies Old Trafford manager graveyard claim amid seven-match winless run - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 26일(월) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Carrick denies Old Trafford manager graveyard claim amid seven-match winless run 
 입력 2026.10.25. 16:21 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Michael Carrick (45), manager of Manchester United, directly rejected negative assessments surrounding the club. Although he has been under pressure over potential dismissal after failing to win in seven consecutive matches, he disagreed with the claim that United is a club where managers cannot succeed.
 The U.K. 'BBC' reported on the 25th (Korea time) that Manchester United manager Michael Carrick dismissed the claim that the club at Old Trafford is a team managers cannot control.
 United are in serious slump. They have not won a single match in seven recent official matches. On the 22nd, they suffered a 1-4 heavy defeat to Como in the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) Champions League match. Carrick himself admitted the performance in that match was an "unacceptable level."
 The home Premier League match against Bournemouth on the 25th is a crucial turning point for Carrick. As consecutive poor results have revealed discontent within the squad to the outside, pressure on the manager has increased.
 Lisandro Martínez and Bruno Fernandes recently made remarks criticizing the club's player recruitment policy and Carrick's tactics. With key players publicly raising issues, the atmosphere around the team has become even more unsettled.
 United have not regained past glories since manager Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. If Carrick steps down, it would be the third managerial change in the past three seasons.
 The BBC noted that including Ralf Rangnick, eight long-term managerial regimes since Ferguson left United the job without meeting expectations have departed the team.
 Added to this are criticisms from famous former United players and the influence of fan channels with large viewerships, leading to assessments that United is an excessively difficult environment for managers.
 Carrick's view was different. Asked whether United is essentially a club where managers cannot succeed, he answered tersely, "No."
 Carrick refuted some criticisms of the team's performance. In particular, he disagreed with the criticism that United players do not run enough and do not press opponents when they do not have possession.
 He explained, "You have to be careful about simply saying the players do not run. We won many games over a period. Pressing is also only a small part of football."
 He added rhetorically, "There are many ways to press. What exactly is pressing? Why do it? Is it to play to our team's strengths, or to cover weaknesses in other areas?"
 Carrick emphasized, "These days the word 'pressing' is used too easily. You do not have to press to win a football match. Sometimes it's necessary, but other times it's not. You cannot judge the content of a match simply by how much the players ran."
 He then said, "We need to do again what we did well in parts of last season and this season."
 There are those supporting Carrick during these difficult times: former managers Ferguson and Ole Gunnar Solskjær, who once led United.
 Carrick was appointed in January as the successor to manager Rúben Amorim. He remains close with Solskjær, who had been mentioned as a managerial candidate at the time.
 Solskjær visited United's training facility in Trondheim, Norway, during the preseason in July and spent time with Carrick and his coaching staff. The two have recently been in contact as well.
 Carrick said he also spoke with Ferguson. He explained, "I speak with both of them quite regularly. There's nothing special. I'm close with both. This week is no different from usual."
 Ferguson was the figure who signed Carrick from Tottenham in 2006. He also took the baton at Carrick's testimonial match at Old Trafford in 2017.
 Carrick expressed belief that he can overcome the current crisis. He said his trust in the squad has not changed.
 He emphasized, "I definitely believe in the players. I trust them 100%."
 He added emphatically, "We must be a different team in the next match. We have to show a changed side."
 Seven matches without a win, public criticism from key players, and persistent dismissal rumors. The situation around United is not easy. But Carrick drew a line against the claim that United is a graveyard for managers.
